h1: Antiterrorism Level 1 Training Quiz & Practice Questions
subhead: Take a free practice quiz or snap a photo of any Antiterrorism Level I (JS-US007) question for an instant, explained answer — finish your annual refresher without getting stuck on a definition.
metaTitle: Antiterrorism Level 1 (JS-US007) Quiz & Practice Q&A | Cambo
metaDescription: Free Antiterrorism Level I Awareness Training quiz and practice questions with instant, explained answers. Get through your annual JS-US007 refresher faster.
whyItWorks: JS-US007 leans heavily on specific definitions and protective-measure categories that are easy to mix up under time pressure. Cambo reads the exact question on your screen and gives you the right answer plus the reasoning, so a fuzzy memory of a term doesn't stall the whole module.

sampleQuestions.q: Which of the following is an example of a physical security measure you can take to protect yourself against terrorism?
options: Posting your travel schedule publicly so colleagues always know where you are
Varying your daily routine — changing your times and routes so you're harder to predict
Always using the same trusted route to and from work
Wearing your ID badge visibly at all times when off the installation
sampleQuestions.a: Varying your daily routine — arriving and leaving at different times and taking different routes makes you a harder target to predict and plan against.

sampleQuestions.q: What is the definition of terrorism used in DoD antiterrorism training?
options: Any criminal act committed by a foreign national on U.S. soil
Any act of violence committed during a declared armed conflict
The unlawful use of violence or threat of violence to instill fear and coerce governments or societies for political, religious, or ideological objectives
Espionage carried out on behalf of a hostile foreign government
sampleQuestions.a: The unlawful use of violence or threat of violence to instill fear and coerce governments or societies, often for political, religious, or ideological objectives.

sampleQuestions.q: What does the acronym FPCON stand for in DoD antiterrorism planning?
options: Force Protection Condition
Federal Personnel Contingency
Facility Perimeter Control
Forward Post Communication
sampleQuestions.a: Force Protection Condition — a graduated threat-level system (Normal, Alpha, Bravo, Charlie, Delta) that dictates specific security measures based on the assessed terrorist threat.

sampleQuestions.q: You notice someone photographing entry points and taking notes near a DoD facility. What should you do?
options: Confront the person directly and ask them to delete the photos
Ignore it — photography from a public area is always lawful
Wait to see whether they return another day before mentioning it
Report it to security or law enforcement as possible pre-attack surveillance
sampleQuestions.a: Report it to security or law enforcement as potential surveillance — documenting entry points and security patterns is a common pre-attack indicator covered in antiterrorism training.

sampleQuestions.q: What is the purpose of the DoD's "See Something, Say Something"-style reporting programs?
options: To encourage personnel to report suspicious activity, since early reporting of seemingly minor observations can help prevent an attack
To collect statistics on how often personnel use installation facilities
To identify personnel who need refresher security training
To document maintenance issues around the installation perimeter
sampleQuestions.a: To encourage personnel to report suspicious activity that could indicate terrorism planning, since early reporting of seemingly minor observations can help prevent an attack.

sampleQuestions.q: Which of the following best describes "target hardening" as an antiterrorism concept?
options: Training personnel in hand-to-hand combat techniques
Relocating a facility to a lower-threat country
Making a facility or individual a less attractive target through barriers, lighting, and access control
Increasing the number of personnel assigned to a facility
sampleQuestions.a: Making a facility or individual a less attractive target by adding physical security measures — barriers, lighting, access control — that increase the difficulty and risk for a potential attacker.

faqs.q: How often do I have to complete Antiterrorism Level 1 training?
faqs.a: Annually — it's a yearly requirement under DoDI 2000.16 for anyone with DoD network or facility access, including contractors.

faqs.q: How long does the training take?
faqs.a: About 2 hours for the full JS-US007 course, though the exact time varies by how quickly you move through the knowledge checks.
Level I is the baseline awareness training required of all DoD personnel. Higher levels (II, III, IV) apply to antiterrorism officers and specialized roles and go well beyond general awareness.

faqs.q: Is Cambo affiliated with the DoD or JKO?
faqs.a: No. Cambo is an independent study tool, not produced or endorsed by the Department of Defense or Joint Knowledge Online.

faqs.q: What topics does the course cover?
faqs.a: Terrorism definitions and threat levels, personal protective measures, recognizing surveillance and suspicious activity, and reporting procedures.

faqs.q: What happens if I don't pass the final knowledge check?
faqs.a: You can typically review the material and retake it — most versions don't cap the number of attempts, just require a passing score before issuing your certificate.
